title: Invoicing Software Comparison for Small Businesses
description: A comparison of invoicing platforms — FreshBooks, QuickBooks, Xero, Stripe Invoicing, PayPal, and Wave — evaluating features, automation, payment processing, and scalability.
body:
Invoicing software has become a critical business tool as organizations move away from manual billing processes. Modern invoicing platforms automate invoice generation, payment collection, reconciliation, and follow-up, reducing the time between service delivery and payment receipt.

This comparison evaluates six invoicing platforms across features, automation capabilities, payment processing, and scalability. Pricing references should be verified against each vendor's current rates.

## FreshBooks

FreshBooks is purpose-built for invoicing and is the most intuitive platform for service-based businesses. Its invoice creation workflow guides users through template selection, line item entry, and customization with minimal friction.

FreshBooks' automation capabilities include recurring invoices, automatic payment reminders, and late payment fees. The platform also provides a client self-service portal where customers can view invoices, make payments, and download receipts.

The platform's per-client pricing model makes it cost-effective for organizations with a manageable number of clients. Service-based businesses with fewer than fifty active clients derive the most value from FreshBooks' pricing structure.

Check FreshBooks' current pricing page for exact rates.

## QuickBooks Online

QuickBooks Online integrates invoicing with full accounting capabilities, making it the right choice for organizations that want a single platform for billing and financial management. Invoices created in QuickBooks flow directly to accounts receivable and the general ledger.

QuickBooks' invoicing features include customizable templates, recurring invoice templates, batch invoice creation, and progress invoicing for project-based billing. Payment processing is integrated through QuickBooks Payments, with funds deposited directly to the linked bank account.

QuickBooks' strength is its accounting depth, not its invoicing-specific user experience. Organizations that prioritize invoicing speed and simplicity over accounting integration may prefer FreshBooks or other invoicing-focused platforms.

Check QuickBooks' current pricing page for exact rates.

## Xero

Xero's invoicing capabilities are comparable to QuickBooks, with a cleaner interface and stronger support for multi-currency invoicing. Xero supports invoices in over 160 currencies, with automatic exchange rate updates and currency-specific templates.

Xero's repeating invoice functionality supports daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly intervals with automatic generation and sending. The platform also provides invoice branding and custom field support for organizations that need tailored invoice content.

Xero's unlimited user pricing is advantageous for organizations with multiple staff who need invoice access. Unlike QuickBooks, which charges per additional user at higher tiers, Xero includes unlimited users across all paid plans.

Check Xero's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Stripe Invoicing

Stripe Invoicing is an API-first billing platform that integrates with the Stripe payment ecosystem. Its strength is customization and automation for organizations with high invoice volume or complex billing models.

Stripe Invoicing supports subscription billing with proration, usage-based billing, and one-time invoices. The platform automatically handles dunning, retries failed payments, and sends smart receipt emails. Stripe's payment infrastructure supports over 135 currencies and multiple payment methods.

Stripe Invoicing is best suited for organizations that already use Stripe for payment processing or have technical resources to configure its API-based platform. Non-technical users may find Stripe's interface less approachable than purpose-built invoicing applications.

Check Stripe's current pricing page for exact rates, as Stripe charges per invoice and per successful payment.

## PayPal Invoicing

PayPal Invoicing leverages PayPal's payment ecosystem and user base to simplify invoice payment. Recipients can pay invoices using PayPal balance, credit cards, or PayPal Credit without creating an account.

PayPal Invoicing includes basic templates, recurring invoices, and payment tracking. Its primary advantage is payment convenience for customers who already use PayPal. The platform's limitations include basic reporting, limited customization, and minimal integration with accounting systems.

Check PayPal's current pricing page for exact rates, as PayPal's fee structure varies by transaction type and currency.

## Wave

Wave offers free invoicing and accounting software for small businesses, generating revenue through payment processing fees. Its pricing model eliminates software subscription costs entirely for organizations that can accept Wave's payment processing rates.

Wave's invoicing features include unlimited invoices, recurring invoices, automatic payment reminders, and mobile invoice creation. The platform also provides receipt scanning and basic accounting capabilities at no cost.

Wave is appropriate for sole proprietors and very small businesses with low invoice volume. As organizations grow, Wave's limited features and support options become constraints that justify paid platform subscriptions.

Check Wave's current pricing page for exact rates, as Wave's pricing model is based on transaction volume rather than software subscription.

## Selection Guidance

The right invoicing platform depends on billing complexity, integration requirements, and growth trajectory. Service-based businesses with straightforward billing benefit from FreshBooks' specialist focus. Organizations needing integrated accounting should evaluate QuickBooks and Xero. High-volume or subscription billing businesses need Stripe Invoicing's API-based automation. Sole proprietors and micro-businesses can leverage Wave's free platform while managing payment processing costs.
